nodes.summary: For continuous `g` and `p ∈ (0, 1)`, the function `u(q) = ∫ x in 0..1, G(q, x) g(x)` solves the neutral backward equation `L_0 u = -g` at `p`. In the diffusion reading, `u(p)` is the expected value of `∫₀^T g(X_t) dt` up to the absorption time `T`.
nodes.title: Green's representation (Ewens 2004, Chapter 4)

nodes.summary: Boundary value at `0`: an allele that is absent spends no time in `(0, 1)`, so `∫ x in 0..1, G(0, x) g(x) = 0`.
nodes.title: Sojourn integral vanishes for an absent allele

nodes.summary: Boundary value at `1`: a fixed allele spends no time in `(0, 1)`, so `∫ x in 0..1, G(1, x) g(x) = 0`.
nodes.title: Sojourn integral vanishes for a fixed allele

nodes.summary: For `p ∈ [0, 1]`, the total expected sojourn time `∫ x in 0..1, G(p, x)` is the Kimura–Ohta mean absorption time `-2 (p log p + (1 - p) log (1 - p))` (units of `2N` generations).
nodes.title: Mean absorption time as a sojourn integral

nodes.summary: The neutral Wright–Fisher Green's function (sojourn density), time in units of `2N` generations (Ewens 2004, Chapter 4): `G(p, x) = 2 (1 - p) / (1 - x)` for `x ≤ p` and `G(p, x) = 2 p / x` for `p < x`. In the diffusion reading, for `0 < x < 1`, `G(p, x) dx` is the expected time a neutral allele started at frequency `p` spends at frequencies in `(x, x + dx)` before loss or fixation.
nodes.title: Neutral Wright–Fisher Green's function
